title: Customer Service Administrator
description:
Customer Service Administrator
Glasgow 16.00 per hour 12-Month Temporary Contract
We're recruiting for a Customer Service Administrator to join a large, well-established organisation in Glasgow. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys administration, problem-solving and delivering a high standard of customer service within a busy operational environment.

This is a predominantly administration-based role with occasional customer contact. You'll be responsible for handling customer requests, reviewing documentation, updating records and supporting a range of operational processes.
Following a comprehensive training programme, hybrid working will be available.

Key Responsibilities
Processing customer requests and ensuring records are updated accurately and efficiently.
Reviewing customer information and documentation to ensure all requirements have been met.
Managing a variety of work queues, customer requests and shared inboxes.
Communicating with customers where necessary to obtain information or provide updates.
Taking ownership of queries from receipt through to resolution.
Supporting the delivery of an excellent customer experience throughout the customer journey.
Maintaining a high level of accuracy when handling data and sensitive information.
Working within established policies, procedures and compliance frameworks.
Identifying and escalating any potential issues or risks where appropriate.
Collaborating with colleagues to achieve team objectives and service level agreements.

About You
We're looking for candidates who are motivated, organised and keen to learn.
You'll ideally have:
Previous administration, customer service or contact centre experience.
Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal.
Good organisational and time management skills.
Confidence using multiple systems and managing a varied workload.
A proactive and positive approach to work.

Desirable, but not essential:
Experience working in a regulated environment.
Previous experience within financial services, insurance or professional services.
Experience handling customer documentation or verification processes.
Exposure to risk, compliance or quality-checking activities.
What's On Offer?
16.00 per hour.
12-month temporary assignment.
Potential opportunity for contract extension or permanent opportunities.
Full training provided.
Initial training period of approximately 4 to 8 weeks in the Glasgow office.
Hybrid working available following successful completion of training, with 2 days in the office and 3 days working from home.
Supportive team environment with ongoing development opportunities.
This role would suit administrators, customer service professionals, operations assistants, claims handlers, coordinators and contact centre advisers looking to develop their experience within a professional and highly structured environment.

Search is an equal opportunities recruiter and we welcome applications from all suitably skilled or qualified applicants, regardless of their race, sex, disability, religion/beliefs, sexual orientation or age

title: Customer Service Administrator - December start date
description:
Are you looking for new opportunity in time for Xmas? If so keep reading as we have a number of exciting positions available with start dates in December this year!

We have a number of opportunities available with scattered intakes across December for someone to join one of the UK's leading banking groups as a Customer Service Administrator. As a Customer Service Administrator you will have meaningful conversations with new and existing customers. You will be point of contact for prospective and existing customers for a range of administrative tasks, providing a fantastic customer experience and play an important role in supporting the team's wider business objectives.
- Hours of work (Training Period) Monday to Friday 9am - 5pm, fully onsite for 8 weeks
- After training period Full Time - Monday - Saturday (Apply online only) (Must be fully flexible)
- Pay Rate 16.00ph
- 12 month contract
- Option to work from home 3 days per week after training period
- Weekly Pay

Please note you must be able to pass a credit check and DBS check and be able to provide 2 years of references.

Duties and Responsibilities will include:
- Manage customer requests to amend their mandates
- Being point of contact for prospective and existing customers for a range of administrative tasks, providing a fantastic customer experience at all times
- Taking ownership of queries and requests
- Contributing to the team's overall business objectives
- Ensuring that service quality is of the highest order, developing measures to continually assess the service provided to clients
- Maintaining and demonstrating high degrees of data quality and accuracy
- Managing different pipelines daily including email inboxes, new requests, returned customer information and internal approvals to maximise the customer experience.
- Assessing the risks of the business and customer and ensuring we make the right decision to keep the business safe.
- Following a contact strategy to make sure our customers are kept informed and engaged at every step of the journey.

To be considered you must have:
- Experience within customer service and a passion to go the extra mile to ensure a brilliant customer experience
- Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage administrative tasks efficiently and work to agreed deadlines.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook and Teams
- Strong verbal and written communication skills
- Experience working within a team dynamic to provide excellent customer experience
- Ability to understand and follow policies and procedures to ensure we keep the society and our customers safe

If you would like to know more, please apply now or contact Darcey at the Glasgow office.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Credit Controller
Competitive Salary
Thornliebank, Glasgow
Full-Time Established Business On-Site
Are you an experienced Credit Controller looking for your next opportunity within an established and supportive finance team?

We are recruiting for a Credit Controller to join a well-established business based in Thornliebank, Glasgow. This is an excellent opportunity for an organised and confident finance professional who enjoys working with customers, managing accounts and playing an important role in maintaining the financial health of a business.
Working as part of an experienced Credit Control team, you will be responsible for managing customer accounts, collecting outstanding payments and helping to minimise credit risk. You will work closely with customers, the Sales team and colleagues across the wider business, building positive relationships while ensuring payments are received within agreed terms.
This position would suit someone who has previous experience in credit control or accounts receivable, takes pride in accuracy and enjoys working within a busy team environment.
Working Hours
Monday to Thursday 9:30 - 17:30.
Friday 9:30 - 16:00.
This role in fully on-site.
What's in it for you?
Generous holiday entitlement.
Company pension scheme.
Free onsite parking.
Opportunity to develop your skills within an established business.
Key Responsibilities
Proactively manage customer accounts and chase outstanding balances by telephone and email.
Agree and monitor payment arrangements in line with company procedures.
Accurately allocate customer payments and prepare and process Direct Debit collections.
Carry out credit checks and assist with the approval and set-up of new customer accounts.
Monitor credit limits, payment terms and overdue balances, identifying and escalating potential credit risks.
Investigate and resolve account queries and payment discrepancies, liaising with customers and the Sales team.
Provide general administrative support to the Credit Control and wider Finance team.
What We're Looking For
Previous experience within Credit Control, Accounts Receivable or Finance Administration.
Confidence communicating with customers, particularly when discussing outstanding payments.
A professional, proactive and methodical approach to work.
Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and Outlook.
A positive team player who can build effective working relationships.

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Hybrid (1 day per week on-site, max 2 days when fully integrated) Free parking

The Payroll Administrator will provide vital business-as-usual (BAU) support to ensure the smooth operation of high-volume payrolls during a major system transition. The organization is currently preparing to migrate from iTrend to Oracle in April/May 2027. You will be responsible for processing multiple payroll runs and managing complex pension schemes.

Key Deliverables
Act as a key payroll focal point to support the team through a critical system migration from iTrent to Oracle.
Deliver consistent, high-volume BAU payroll processing for approximately 5,000 staff across 3 monthly payrolls.
Administer and coordinate complex pension schemes, specifically managing Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS) and Teachers' Pensions.
Resolve complex pay and pension queries in an efficient and timely manner to support employee wellbeing and engagement.
Manage the payroll workflow end-to-end, including processing new starters, leavers, structural changes, and contract variations.
Receive, verify, and input employee absence, sickness, and statutory payment records.
Process holiday requests, overtime claims, and manual payroll adjustments for payment processing.
Investigate and correct timesheet and payment errors, escalating system anomalies as required.
Maintain accurate and detailed logs of all personnel queries and payroll adjustments to ensure robust audit trails during the transition period.

Key Requirements / Qualifications
Education: Relevant payroll qualification (CIPP or equivalent) or demonstrated capability via extensive hands-on experience.
IT Skills: Solid IT skills across the MS Office Suite, including strong Excel and data analysis capabilities.
Experience: Previous experience managing high-volume payrolls within a complex, multi-payroll environment. Experience handling roughly 5,000 records across multiple monthly cycles is highly advantageous.
System Knowledge: Prior experience utilizing iTrent or Oracle payroll software is highly desirable, though not strictly non-negotiable.
Pension Knowledge: Demonstrable experience working with public sector pension schemes, specifically LGPS and Teachers' Pensions, is highly preferred.
Industry Knowledge: Previous experience working within a College, University, Local Council, or broader Public Sector environment is highly desirable.
Communication: Clear and confident communicator at all levels, capable of explaining complex payroll and pension queries face-to-face, via email, and over the telephone.

52570 AD

INDPAYN

The Portfolio Group are acting on behalf of our client in recruiting for this position.

title: Repairs Administrator
description:
Currently recruiting for a Repairs Administrator to join a well-established housing association in Glasgow on an initial 6-month temporary contract.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an organised, customer-focused individual to join a busy Property Services team, supporting the delivery of reactive repairs, maintenance and void property services.

We're keen to hear from candidates with experience in repairs administration, maintenance coordination, property services or customer service, particularly those who enjoy working in a busy environment and managing multiple priorities.

The Role

Working as part of the Property Services team, you'll be responsible for providing administrative and customer service support across reactive repairs and void maintenance.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Handling incoming repairs enquiries by telephone, email and in person.
- Logging repairs and raising works orders on the housing management system.
- Coordinating appointments and inspections for Maintenance Officers.
- Liaising with contractors, tenants and utility companies to ensure repairs progress efficiently.
- Monitoring void property repairs and supporting the turnaround of empty properties.
- Updating maintenance records, compliance information and property databases.
- Assisting with contractor invoices and general administration.
- Logging customer complaints and supporting customer satisfaction processes.
- Providing administrative support to the wider Property Services team.

About You

We're looking for someone who has:
- Previous experience in administration, repairs coordination, property maintenance or a similar customer-focused role.
- Excellent communication and organisational skills.
- The ability to manage a busy workload and prioritise effectively.
- Strong IT skills and experience using CRM or database systems.
- A proactive, helpful approach and excellent attention to detail.
- The ability to work confidently with customers, contractors and colleagues.

Previous social housing experience would be advantageous, particularly experience using QL or other housing management systems. However, candidates with strong transferable skills from property maintenance, facilities management or customer service environments are also encouraged to apply.

What's on Offer?
- Salary of 27,068 per annum
- 35-hour working week
- Initial 6-month temporary contract
- Opportunity to gain valuable experience within the social housing sector
- Supportive and friendly working environment

Interested?

If you're an experienced administrator looking for your next opportunity, we'd love to hear from you!

Apply today with your CV, or contact Laura at RG Setsquare for a confidential chat.

Applications close Monday 9 November 2026, with interviews expected Monday 16 November 2026.

RG Setsquare is acting as an Employment Business in relation to this vacancy.

title: Receptionist / Front of house
description:
An opportunity has arisen for a Receptionist / Front of house to join a legal practice, providing professional legal services and maintaining an efficient and welcoming office environment.

As a Receptionist, you will take primary responsibility for reception and front-of-house activities, welcoming visitors, handling telephone enquiries and ensuring the smooth running of the reception area.

title: Customer Service Advisor
description:
Customer Service Advisor

Red Recruitment is recruiting a Customer Service Advisor to join our client's Customer Financial Assistance and Recoveries team in Glasgow.

You will support customers with car finance enquiries, including ending agreements early and managing the next steps when a vehicle has been written off. Combining telephone support with administration and casework, you will guide customers through sensitive situations with empathy, clarity and care.

This is a permanent opportunity, with the option to work hybrid after six months.

Benefits and Package for a Customer Service Advisor:
- Salary: 13.30 per hour
- Hours: Shifts worked on a rolling rota within Monday - Friday, 8am - 6pm, and Saturday, 9am - 5pm
- Contract Type: Permanent
- Location: Glasgow, office-based initially with the option to work hybrid after six months

Key Responsibilities of a Customer Service Advisor:
- Handling incoming calls from customers looking to end their car finance agreement early
- Explaining eligibility, the process and any outstanding payments clearly and accurately
- Supporting customers whose vehicles have been written off, liaising with insurance companies and providing settlement figures
- Recognising vulnerable customers and those experiencing financial difficulties, ensuring they receive appropriate support
- Processing paperwork, updating customer records and maintaining accurate case notes
- Following up on enquiries and arranging vehicle collections with partner suppliers
- Identifying complaints and following the appropriate procedures to ensure fair customer outcomes

Skills and Experience of a Customer Service Advisor:
- Excellent customer service and communication skills, with confidence handling sensitive or challenging conversations
- An empathetic approach and good judgement when supporting customers in difficult circumstances
- The ability to explain complex information in a clear and straightforward way
- Strong attention to detail and accurate administration skills
- Confidence navigating multiple systems and managing follow-up tasks
- A minimum of six months' financial services experience is advantageous but not essential

If you have the relevant skills and are interested in this position, please apply now!

title: Call Centre Agent
description:
Start date: 25.01.2027

Shift Pattern: Full Time (37.5 hours)

Please note that this position is a full-time role only, and part-time hours are not available.

Sales Advisors

If you're outgoing, full of energy and love talking to people, you'd be better off in sales with EE.

Maybe you've worked in retail, or hospitality before. You know how to deal with customers but you're looking for something more exciting - a job that's going to challenge you. And, of course, you want to earn a bit more cash.

Our Glasgow team's full of people like you - so you'll be in great company here.

What does being a sales advisor involve?

You'll join a lively sales team in our Glasgow contact centre. We'll train you to take incoming calls from existing EE customers and help them find the best deals on their phones and broadband. You'll also help them to navigate the different tech products we sell.

You need to be a great listener as well as a fluent talker. A lot of the time, you'll pick up on something that someone has said, then use that to match them with the perfect product.

Forget what you've heard about sales

Don't let what you've heard about sales put you off. Let's smash a few myths
- Yes, there are targets to hit. But the kind of people who like sales, love that. You're probably naturally competitive. You get a buzz out of beating the person next to you. You hate being bored at work.
- It's not "cold calling". The calls come in to you and you decide how best you can help the customer. That's why we value resourceful people who like fixing problems.
- People say it's "hard selling". It's really not! You're basically talking to people about fun tech stuff that they already want. Who doesn't love a better phone, faster broadband or a new console?

Why you'll be better off at EE

GREAT MONEY - you start on £26,116 which goes up to £26,738 after 8 months.

UNCAPPED COMMISSION - the more you sell, the more you can earn.

BRILLIANT BENEFITS - including 24/7 GP appointments for you and your family, discounted parking and discounts on EE products like phones and broadband that could save you £100s every year.

GROWTH - we're passionate about developing our people. There are plenty of career paths across EE and BT.

FLEXIBILITY - you can bank hours then take time off when you need. Plus, generous leave for carers and anyone starting a family.

GREAT PEOPLE - you're working with people like you. It's a sociable, supportive environment.

title: Recruitment Administrator - Immediate Start
description:
Recruitment Administrator - 6 month contract
Glasgow City Centre - Hybrid working available after training
Monday to Friday, 35 hours per week
Pay Rate 17.47ph

About the Role

We are seeking a highly organised and proactive Recruitment Administrator to support a busy, high-volume recruitment team. This role is responsible for coordinating and administering the full end-to-end recruitment process, ensuring vacancies are filled efficiently while delivering an excellent experience for candidates, hiring managers, and stakeholders.

Working in a fast-paced and often high-pressure environment, the successful candidate will manage multiple recruitment campaigns simultaneously, maintain accurate records, and ensure compliance with company policies and recruitment procedures.

Key Responsibilities
Recruitment Coordination
- Manage the end-to-end recruitment administration process across multiple vacancies
- Coordinate job postings across internal and external recruitment platforms
- Screen and process applications in line with agreed recruitment criteria
- Schedule and coordinate interviews & assessment centres
- Liaise with candidates throughout the recruitment lifecycle, providing timely updates and maintaining a positive candidate experience
- Support recruiters and hiring managers with recruitment activities and vacancy management

Compliance and Onboarding
- Ensure all recruitment activities comply with company policies, employment legislation, and data protection requirements.
- Conduct pre-employment checks, including right-to-work verification, reference requests, and background screening.
- Prepare offer documentation and employment contracts where applicable.
- Coordinate onboarding activities to ensure a smooth transition from candidate to employee.

Key Skills and Experience
Essential
- Previous experience in a recruitment, HR administration, or talent acquisition support role.
- Experience supporting high-volume recruitment campaigns across multiple vacancies.
- Strong administrative and organisational skills with exceptional attention to detail.
- Ability to work effectively under pressure and manage competing priorities.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Outlook, Excel, Word, and Teams.
- Experience using Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) or recruitment management systems.
- Strong customer service focus with the ability to build positive relationships at all levels.

Key Competencies
- Planning and organising
- Attention to detail
- Managing competing priorities
- Customer and candidate focus
- Stakeholder engagement
- Problem solving
- Teamwork and collaboration
- Resilience and adaptability
- Communication and influencing skills

title: MEICA Project Administrator
description:
Love being the person who keeps everything on track? This one's for you.

We're pumping and water treatment specialists, and we're part of a €200m group with 800 employees and sites across the UK and Eire. We deliver the mechanical, electrical, instrumentation, control and automation (MEICA) work behind the water and wastewater infrastructure that communities rely on every day. Our engineering delivery team is growing, and we're looking for an organised, proactive Project Administrator to be the hub that holds our projects together.

Where you come in

You'll be the main point of contact for site engineers, project managers, clients and subcontractors. You'll support our MEICA projects from the first day on site right through to handover. No two days will look quite the same, and you'll see the difference your work makes on real infrastructure projects.

What you'll be doing
- Supporting Project Managers and Site Supervisors across several live MEICA contracts
- Making site mobilisation go smoothly: booking plant hire and accommodation, and ordering specialist PPE
- Tracking timesheets, holidays and subcontractor attendance for payroll and commercial reporting
- Organising and minuting weekly progress meetings, and following action points through to completion
- Keeping project folders accurate and up to date
- Pulling together O&M manuals, asset data sheets and test certificates
- Managing version control and distribution of drawings, RAMS and site permits
- Raising purchase orders, matching delivery notes to invoices, and sorting out supplier discrepancies
- Maintaining cost trackers and helping with monthly valuations
- Tracking training records and expiry dates (CSCS, EUSR Water Hygiene, DOMS, Confined Spaces, First Aid)
- Filing safety audits, inductions and near-miss reports so we stay compliant with ISO and client framework requirements

What you'll bring
- Experience in project administration, site coordination or document control, ideally in MEICA, construction, civils or utilities
- Strong Microsoft Office skills, especially Excel, Word and SharePoint
- Great organisation, and you're calm when several deadlines land at once
- A sharp eye for detail
- Confidence talking to anyone, from site operatives to suppliers and clients

Bonus points for
- Knowing your way around H&S documentation (RAMS, Permits to Work) and EUSR cards
- A Business Administration qualification (NVQ Level 3, HNC or equivalent)

Why join us?

You'll get the stability and scale of a major group with sites across the UK and Eire. You'll also work in a close-knit delivery team where your contribution is seen and valued. Our work is meaningful and our projects are varied, and there's real room to grow your career in a sector that matters.

Ready to be the engine room of our projects? Apply today. We'd love to hear from you.

title: Technical Project Coordinator, LED & Video Events
description:
Neo Recruitment is working with a Scottish live events technology business that delivers LED, video and graphics playout for major occasions across Scotland, England and Europe. They are looking for a Technical Project Coordinator who is as comfortable planning at a desk as they are troubleshooting on site.

The role

You will take an enquiry or a client handover and turn it into a clear plan, a clear job sheet and clear expectations for the freelancers delivering it. Then you will make sure it happens, mostly from the office and warehouse, and on site for the larger projects. It is a hands-on role with real ownership, and the standards you set will shape how every event is run.

Around 70% of your time will be based at the office and warehouse, and around 30% on project work, typically 2 to 5 day jobs. That includes travel across Scotland and England, and to Europe when a job requires it.

What you will be doing
- Building enquiries from a general concept through to project planning and delivery
- Turning client handover information, such as playlists, media assets and emails, into clear job sheets
- Creating production documents for each event, using lessons from past jobs
- Testing playout projects and distributing them to the teams who will run them
- Crewing events and managing freelancers on the ground
- Leading installation and commissioning across Scotland, England and, where necessary, Europe
- Tracking crew, subcontractor and technical purchasing costs, and supporting asset management in the warehouse

Who we would like to meet
- A technical background across hardware and software
- Good events industry experience, on site and in production operations
- Substantial LED and video experience, which is strongly preferred
- Experience of directing freelancers or subcontractors
- Practical troubleshooting skills and the ability to stay steady when events get busy
- Willingness to travel across Scotland and England, and to Europe when required
- vMix or live graphics experience would be a valuable bonus
- Based in or within commuting distance of the Glasgow area

If your background is in a neighbouring area of live events or AV and you have the hands-on skills, we would still like to hear from you.

What is on offer
- A permanent, full time role with genuine ownership from first enquiry to delivery
- Variety across the office, warehouse and live event sites
- The chance to shape freelancer standards and the way events are planned and documented

Next steps

Send us your CV and we will arrange a one hour Teams call: 15 minutes about the opportunity and the company, and 45 minutes about you. Your details are never shared without your permission. You must have the right to work in the UK.
